jeeves.where: module-clients.ts.template (externalTarget: 'the client reads no credential'); jeeves-generator README
jeeves.gap: An External API client has no workload-identity credential. A stub that calls a Google API (Web Risk) can only add a header itself; the documented way is a credential from a SECRET_DIR file, i.e. a long-lived API key. On Cloud Run, Link API's Q06 code got 403 from Web Risk and every guest create failed closed (503).
jeeves.workaround: Application files: link-operations/google-credentials.ts fetches Link API's service-account token from the metadata server (cached, monotonic, one deadline with the lookup) when QRWTY_REPUTATION_CREDENTIALS=metadata; the production profile requires that value. 9 unit tests.

jeeves.gap: Tile-to-tile calls carry no ID token, so Cloud Run's invoker IAM can't protect a service another tile calls: such a service must be internal-only with IAM off, and any VPC caller can reach it. A public origin can be IAM-protected only if no tile calls it (Billing API had to become internal; Stripe webhooks would need it public).
jeeves.workaround: IaC: internal ingress with IAM off for Link, Account and Billing API; IAM required for the public Redirect and Session origins (no allUsers).

jeeves.gap: The generated health route /healthz is a path Cloud Run's front end reserves: <service>.run.app/healthz answers Google's 404 page before the container. Only Cloud Run's own startup and liveness probes reach it, so no edge, uptime check or tile can read a process's health over HTTP.
jeeves.workaround: None needed for this deploy (Cloud Run's probes work); P09 used the sign-in me routes to show reachability.

jeeves.where: module-clients.ts.template (pubsubPublisher, pubsubLoop: new PubSub without apiEndpoint)
jeeves.gap: The Pub/Sub clients always use the global endpoint and have no regional-endpoint binding. The durable-clicks contract pins storage to us-central1 with in-transit enforcement; Pub/Sub then refuses any request the global endpoint routes to another region (FAILED_PRECONDITION, seen from outside the region). The generated publisher and worker work only because Google routes them to us-central1.
jeeves.workaround: None in the app; operators pull dead letters through https://us-central1-pubsub.googleapis.com/. Remedy: JEEVES_PUBSUB_ENDPOINT, required when the topic enforces in transit.

jeeves.gap: A process logs 'Application ready' but nothing when SIGTERM arrives, when its drain starts or ends, or with what code it exits; Cloud Run logs no exit for a service instance either. A rollout's drain can't be shown from logs (P10).
jeeves.workaround: P10 shows the drain by traffic instead: 1,501 requests during the rollout, none failed.

deployment.finding: Q04b: tofu validate passed at once; only tofu fmt failed (locals.tf alignment).
deployment.fix: tofu fmt; validate.sh exits 0 (fmt 0, init 0, validate 0); lint self-test 8/8.

deployment.finding: A CLUSTER_DISABLED Memorystore instance reports no discovery_endpoints (deprecated, empty). The first apply created all 93 resources' worth of stores but failed evaluating the cache variables, so 24 secret IAM bindings and the outputs were never applied.
deployment.fix: locals.cache_primary: the PSC auto connection of type CONNECTION_TYPE_PRIMARY (address and port); outputs use it.

deployment.finding: Each Memorystore instance has its own managed CA (GOOGLE_MANAGED_PER_INSTANCE_CA); the IaC had one CA secret from hot-routes, which Link API's admission-cache would have refused.
deployment.fix: One public CA secret per cache (qrwtya-memorystore-ca-<cache>), mounted for the one process that uses it; the probe shows the other instance's CA is refused.

deployment.finding: The migration job had no VPC egress: the Cloud SQL connector couldn't reach the private-only instance and both first executions timed out (pg 'timeout expired' after 5 s, uncaught).
deployment.fix: vpc_access (Direct VPC egress, ALL_TRAFFIC) on the job, as on the services.

deployment.finding: Cloud Run's Direct VPC egress with ALL_TRAFFIC leaves no Internet route: Auth0's key set, the tenant origin and Stripe need a NAT. Added before the first apply. Measured: a fresh task's first connection through the NAT failed for 12 s and 48 s in two runs, a second destination for about 4 s; Google APIs over Private Google Access worked at once.
deployment.fix: qrwtya-router and qrwtya-nat (AUTO_ONLY, the run subnet only).

deployment.finding: Pub/Sub reads the archive (Cloud Storage) subscription's ack deadline back as 300 s; the IaC said 60, a perpetual diff.
Cloud Run returns secret volumes before the Cloud SQL volume; the IaC's order made every plan show a reorder of all six resources.
deployment.fix: Secret volumes and mounts first; the final plan reports no changes.

deployment.finding: The services declared no traffic block, so P11's manual pin (gcloud --no-traffic) survived the image-2 apply: Session API kept serving image 1 with a dangling tag.
deployment.fix: traffic { LATEST 100 } on every service; the next apply moved Session API to its latest revision and dropped the tag.

deployment.finding: Billing API was public (for Stripe webhooks through the edge), but tile clients can't authenticate to an IAM-protected origin (AG-14) and no edge exists in this release.
deployment.fix: Billing API internal; public origins (Redirect, Session) require Cloud Run IAM. The qrwty.io Worker route was not added: it would need proxy code, not only a route, and an edge credential the origin can verify.

deployment.finding: Additions the Q06 handoff asked for and the cloud needs.
deployment.fix: Secret link-replay-keys (mounted for Link API), QRWTY_PUBLIC_ORIGIN_URL = https://qrwty.io, webrisk.googleapis.com in the API list, QRWTY_REPUTATION_CREDENTIALS = metadata with image 2.
